newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's Teva Q4 EPS $0.49 V 0.31.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Teva Q4 EPS $0.49 V 0.31.

text.p: Teva said fourth-quarter 1995 earnings did not include a one-time expense equal to $0.07 a share after tax taken after writing off the debt of an Israeli health maintenance organisation. The 1996 full-year earnings per share (EPS) did not include one-time expenses of $0.24 a share after tax in connection with its acquisition of Biocraft Laboratories Inc.
Teva said its board had voted to increase the fourth-quarter dividend to 0.30 shekel per share from 0.20 shekel in each of the previous three quarters and in the the year-earlier quarter.
The company said EPS figures were based on its 0.1 share.

"This was the most important year in the company's history -- a year in which we graduated to a new league," Teva president and CEO Eli Hurvitz said at a news conference, citing U.S. Food and Drug Administration approval for the company's first proprietary drug, Copaxone.
Teva said marketing for Copaxone, a multiple sclerosis treatment, would begin in the current quarter in the U.S. Approvals from various European health authorities were expected over the year.
The company said in a statement that the global consolidation of the pharmaceuticals industry required it to be on the lookout for merger and joint venture opportunities.
"Our next goal of remaining a leader in the generic market requires us to grow at home and to buy other companies both in the United States and Europe," said Hurvitz.
He said Teva's U.S. unit was one of the three largest generic drug makers in the country and that it aspired to be a leader in the European market as well.
Teva noted that a quarter of its sales came from companies acquired in the last two years.
Chief financial officer Dan Seusskind said Teva planned to make a bond offering in the second half. He said the issue would be for more than $100 million and for a term of at least five years.
